content: Cross-platform float determinism is not guaranteed by IEEE-754 alone (non-associative ops, differing compilers/instruction sets). Established practice (FLiT framework, Bruce Dawson's writings) is a hybrid comparator: absolute-difference check first (typical cross-hardware/compiler noise ~5e-15 for doubles), then a ULP-distance check with a small max-ULP threshold (e.g. 4) if the absolute check fails; either passing counts as equal. True bit-exact cross-platform agreement requires restricting to strict IEEE mode and a fixed op set, at a performance cost.
